evidence: CancelOrderUseCase, DeliverOrderUseCase, GetOrderUseCase, PackOrderUseCase, PayOrderUseCase and ShipOrderUseCase all inject OrderLookupService and call this.lookup.getById(orderId), so the order not-found rule is centralized.

CancelOrderUseCase.execute, ShipOrderUseCase.execute and PlaceOrderUseCase.execute all call this.allocations.load(...), then this.reservation.release/commit/reserve, then this.allocations.persist(...), so the stock rules stay in StockAllocationService and StockReservationService.
State changes go through domain methods (order.cancel, order.deliver, order.pack, order.pay, order.ship, Order.place), not checks inside the use cases.
Every use case returns its result through the shared mappers toOrderDto or toProductStockDto.
GetProductStockUseCase.execute is the only by-id product lookup in the unit (products.findById plus a NotFoundError throw), so the rule is not duplicated within the module.
ListOrdersUseCase.execute calls OrderRepository.findByStatus/findAll directly, which suits a collection query, and PlaceOrderUseCase creates a new order and has nothing to look up.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All ten files hold one application concern: order and product-stock use cases. Each is a class with a single execute method that returns DTOs built by the shared mappers toOrderDto and toProductStockDto. The use cases that fetch an existing order by id all go through OrderLookupService.getById (Cancel, Deliver, Get, Pack, Pay, Ship), so the not-found rule for orders lives in one place. The use cases that change stock follow the same steps through StockAllocationService.load/persist and StockReservationService (reserve, release or commit), and the stock rules stay in those services, not in the use cases. Order state changes are delegated to the domain methods order.pay, pack, ship, deliver and cancel, so no use case re-checks state transitions itself. Some calls skip the lookup service, but each one fits its job: ListOrdersUseCase calls OrderRepository.findByStatus/findAll because it is a collection query, and PlaceOrderUseCase creates a new order. GetProductStockUseCase does its own findById plus NotFoundError check. This is the only by-id product lookup in the unit, so nothing is duplicated within the module. PlaceOrderUseCase.mergeLines is a private helper used in one place, and nothing shown duplicates it. Import direction is out of scope.
